clue.text: Daughter following layabout around with swindler

parts.note: f. is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the idler is placed around the daughter, holding her letter inside

parts.note: a layabout is an idler
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl takes up with an idle good-for-nothing who is also a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the D inside IDLER to give IDDLER, and F for 'following' goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to cheat, so a fiddler in slang is a cheat or petty con artist.

clue.text: Disrepute en famille, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the French word famille is only one possible ordering of its letters, inviting a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Is there scandal within the family circle?
explanation.walkthrough: 'en famille' is French for 'within the family'; only FAMILLE is rearranged, 'en' being a link to keep the French phrase intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill repute or bad reputation is disrepute, a standard dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Indian scrubber died in Delhi after the Spanish left

indicators.note: the letters for died are placed in what remains of Delhi
left here means departed, so the Spanish article quits the word Delhi

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
ob., from Latin obiit, is the abbreviation for died on tombstones and in records

explanation.surface: An Indian cleaner passed away in Delhi once the Spaniards had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing EL from DELHI leaves DHI, and OB goes into it: D-H-OB-I.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a dhobi is a washerman, someone who scrubs clothes for a living.

clue.text: Sheep sacrificed before us here at Artemis's temple

indicators.note: before places the shuffled sheep ahead of the word us
sacrificed suggests the sheep is cut up on the altar, so its letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal offering is made in front of us at an ancient Greek shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is the definition: the answer names the place where Artemis's temple stood. 'sacrificed' fits the surface of an altar offering but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus, in Asia Minor, was the site of the great Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders, so it is the place meant by here.

clue.text: Errant hero offering to capture what's raised in Pandemonium

annotationWithheld.why: Errant hero offering to capture what's raised in Pandemonium (3,4): THE ROOF is defined, but no parse found for the letters T, O, F outside HERO; 'offering to capture' gives no clean container
annotationWithheld.clue: Errant hero offering to capture what's raised in Pandemonium

clue.text: A measure adopted by prince of the blood

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken in, so the prince's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V
an em is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A unit is taken up by a royal heir of noble blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the blood' looks like a description of royalty, but it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Haemal is a medical adjective meaning relating to the blood or blood vessels.

clue.text: I burn rubbish in stratagem to define city farming

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the word for a stratagem

parts.note: a ruse is a stratagem or trick

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb or adjective suggests the letters are poor and must be reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone burning refuse as part of a scheme to describe urban agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' rearranges I BURN into INURB, which goes 'in' RUSE: RUS-INURB-E. The surface picture of burning rubbish hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rus in urbe is a Latin tag meaning the country in the town, a rural feel created within a city.

clue.text: Tissue fold topping driving force

indicators.note: topping means removing the top, so the first letter of the word comes off

parts.note: momentum is the driving force behind something

explanation.surface: A fold of tissue placed on top of a strong impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like a position word but means beheading MOMENTUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The omentum is a fold of the peritoneum, the membrane tissue hanging from the stomach.

clue.text: 1 from La Paz, methinks, right for southern revolution

definitions.note: the clue at 1 across is a violinist, of which this man is a famous example

indicators.note: revolution suggests letters turned and churned, so the whole collection is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: right, R, replaces southern, S, in the word methinks

explanation.surface: Someone from Bolivia's capital muses about rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right for southern' changes METHINKS to METHINKR; 'revolution' then rearranges LA PAZ plus METHINKR into the violinist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Itzhak Perlman is a celebrated violinist, and fiddler is the informal word for a violin player.

clue.text: Call in on the odd characters who inspired Macaulay?

indicators.note: odd characters are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters counted along the words

explanation.surface: A visit to some eccentrics who gave a famous writer ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' looks like strange people; it means the letters at odd positions in CALL IN ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is the Muse of history, so she would inspire the historian Thomas Babington Macaulay.

clue.text: Illegal settler disturbing fodder for Guardian politico

indicators.note: the jumbled settler disturbs the hay by getting in among its letters

parts.note: hay is animal fodder

indicators.note: an illegal settler is wrongly placed, so the word settler is rearranged

explanation.surface: Squatters on land are upsetting the feed meant for a newspaper's politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illegal' is the anagram signal on 'settler', not part of the definition; the politician wrote a Guardian column, hence 'Guardian politico'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Hattersley, the Labour politician, wrote a long-running column for the Guardian.

clue.text: Space station landing in step with 5 of the 25

indicators.note: the space station lands inside the dance step

parts.note: a pas is a step in ballet
Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station

explanation.surface: A space station comes down in time with something on top of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 and 25 are the answers THE ROOF and WORLD, giving the roof of the world, the traditional name for this range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pamirs, a high Central Asian range, are traditionally called the Roof of the World.

clue.text: The tone of a memo from the principal

definitions.meaning: the opening scent or sound, a top note that sets the tone
read in two parts: a note from the head of a school or firm

explanation.definitionFit: A headnote is a summary note at the head of a document, and also the first scent note of a perfume.

clue.text: Shaker put movement into ballet

indicators.note: movement signals that the letters of the two words are moved about

explanation.surface: A rattle was given some motion inside a dance piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like a dance move; it rearranges SHAKER PUT. 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrushka is Stravinsky's ballet about a puppet brought to life.

clue.text: Artist way, way off one of Haile Selassie's styles

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
something way off is afar
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter takes a long journey far from an emperor's title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' gives ST and 'way off' gives AFAR; the repeated word is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari, a title meaning Prince Tafari, was Haile Selassie's style before he became emperor.

clue.text: Cold frost Inspector Frost's scene?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A frosty spell turns up on a TV detective's patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Frost is the detective in the British TV series A Touch of Frost.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective works in the world of crime, so that is his scene or sphere of activity.

clue.text: Society wearing fur in the city

indicators.note: the society letter is dressed in the fur, held inside it

parts.note: mink is a valuable fur

explanation.surface: Fashionable people put on furs in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts S inside MINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Minsk is the capital city of Belarus.

parts.note: fill the gap in the song title If ... a Rich Man (20 down), sung in the musical Fiddler on the Roof (1 across on 5 across)

explanation.definitionFit: The words complete the song title If I Were a Rich Man from the musical Fiddler on the Roof.

clue.text: The Camra Corporation?

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, and CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, so this is the paunch of a real-ale drinker

explanation.definitionFit: A paunch built by drinking ale is a big stomach, and corporation is humorous old slang for such a stomach.

clue.text: Dives in March storms

indicators.note: storms as a verb suggests wild disturbance, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone plunges into the sea during March gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dives' looks like a verb; it is the Latin name given to the wealthy man in the parable of Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives, Latin for wealthy, is the traditional name of the rich man in Jesus's parable of Lazarus.

clue.text: Bacon's Orlando Furioso

definitions.note: read as bacon is, a noun for the cured meat

indicators.note: furioso, furious in Italian, suggests the letters of the name are thrown into a frenzy

explanation.surface: Francis Bacon's take on Ariosto's epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like Francis Bacon the writer; the 's is 'is' linking the meat to the anagram. Orlando Furioso is Ariosto's Italian epic.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardoon is a strip of fat bacon threaded through meat before cooking.

clue.text: Divine wisdom subsequently dividing adults

indicators.note: the word for subsequently splits the pair of adult letters

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adults, so two of them make AA
then means subsequently

explanation.surface: Godly insight later separates grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: THEN sits between the two As.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom, so she is wisdom made divine.

clue.text: Departs work in personal improvement, left with two fingers

indicators.note: the leaving and work letters go inside the home improvement letters

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is improvement done personally
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
an act is a deed or piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone quits a self-help job, leaving with a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two fingers' suggests a rude British gesture; the definition is literal, having two digits.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactyl is a zoological term for having two digits on each limb.

clue.text: One won't put a toe in the water? Lower away, as it were!

definitions.text: One won't put a toe in the water?
definitions.meaning: someone too timid to take the plunge or try anything risky
a lower is a cow that lows, and the suffix -ward means heading in a direction, so this is a jokey cow-direction word

explanation.definitionFit: A faint-hearted person afraid to try anything new is a craven type; split, the word also reads as moving cowwards.

clue.text: It was created with latitude in the scriptures

indicators.note: the latitude letter sits in the scriptural term

parts.note: the Word is the scriptures, the Word of God

explanation.surface: Something made with freedom, as the holy writ describes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' seems to mean freedom; it is just L, which goes inside WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the earth and all creation were made by God, so the planet is the thing created.

clue.text: A few germs a problem for the treatment plant

indicators.note: a problem suggests things are amiss, so the letters are in disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A handful of bacteria cause trouble at a sanitation works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges A FEW GERMS A; 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewage farm is a plant where sewage is treated, often spread on land.

clue.text: Back one to enter the height of success!

indicators.note: one is made to enter the turned word, going inside it
back here means turning the word for a hill backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky height or hill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Support someone who reaches the top of achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns TOR into ROT, and I goes in: R-I-OT. 'Back' looks like support, the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot in the theatrical sense is a smash hit, a great success.

clue.text: Tom Jones's coiffeuse?

parts.note: Tom Jones had a hit song named after a woman, and the biblical woman of that name cut Samson's hair

explanation.definitionFit: Delilah, Samson's betrayer, had his hair cut off, making her a hairdresser of sorts, and is the title of a Tom Jones hit.

clue.text: Done any other sedative?

indicators.note: other suggests a different form of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Have you taken any other calming drug?
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges DONE ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkilling or soothing drug, hence a sedative.
